label: Open door
name: What's on your mind?
description: Undirected, casual, invites any topic without setting an agenda. MBS Kickstart Question.

hints.text: Ask it, then say nothing. This one only works with silence after it.
Whatever they raise first, before anything steers them.
Whether it is work at all.

label: Their agenda
name: What would you most like to talk about today?
description: Hands full agenda ownership to them. Pure person-centered opener — nothing is presupposed.

hints.text: Mean it. If they pick something you did not plan for, go there.
Whether they have something ready or defer back to you.
Whether their topic is on your list too.

label: Real check-in
name: How are you — really?
description: 'Really' subverts the ritual. One word signals this is a different kind of conversation.

hints.text: The really is the question. Let it land before you fill the gap.
Whether the second answer differs from the first.
Whether they answer about themselves or about the work.

label: Energy read
name: What's been giving you energy lately?
description: Strengths-based, not scoped to work. Reveals what genuinely animates the person.

hints.text: Ask about energy, not achievements. Do not turn it into a progress check.
Whether anything comes to mind at all.
Whether what lifts them is the work or the people.

label: What to push on
name: What feels worth pushing on right now?
description: Growth-fitted opener. Surfaces what the report is actively choosing to develop, not what's drifting.

hints.text: Ask what is worth it, not what is urgent. The wording matters.
Whether their answer matches where their time actually goes.
Whether they name one thing or hedge across everything.

label: Since we spoke
name: What's been on your mind since we last spoke?
description: Acknowledges the relationship and the gap between conversations. Open and non-evaluative.

hints.text: Ask it warm and open. It is a door, not a status request.
Whether they pick up a thread from last time or start fresh.
What they choose to lead with.

label: Useful to you
name: What would make this a really useful conversation for you?
description: Positions them as expert on their own needs. Research shows this dramatically improves engagement.

hints.text: Ask before your agenda, not after. Afterwards it reads as a formality.
Whether they can name what would help, or say anything is fine.
Whether their answer shifts what you had planned.

label: What's alive
name: What's been alive for you lately?
description: 'Alive' invites vitality and the whole person — broader than 'what's on your mind', no work scope.

hints.text: Keep it light. It is an opener, not a probe.
Whether the answer comes from work or from outside it.
How long it takes them to find one.

label: Last couple of weeks
name: How has the last couple of weeks felt from your side?
description: Bi-weekly pulse without performative intimacy. Invites an honest read without 'the real version' audition framing.

hints.text: Ask about how it felt, not what happened. Redirect once if they list tasks.
Whether they describe the fortnight or just the last two days.
Whether the feeling matches the delivery you have seen.

label: Bit of joy
name: What's brought you a bit of joy recently?
description: 'A bit of' removes pressure to perform happiness. PERMA positive emotion — activates openness.

hints.text: Ask it and let it be small. A small answer is a real answer.
Whether anything comes easily, or nothing does.
Whether they need to make it work-related to justify it.

label: Head space
name: What's been taking up the most space in your head this week?
description: Spatial metaphor is more honest than 'what's on your mind'. Weight implies it matters.

hints.text: Ask about head space, not workload. They are different questions.
Whether the thing taking the space is the thing they are paid to do.
Whether it is one thing or everything at once.

label: What you're carrying
name: What are you carrying into this conversation?
description: Acknowledges people are not clean slates. Non-evaluative — carrying could be burden or gift.

hints.text: Ask it slowly. It gives permission to name something heavy.
Whether they arrive with something specific or say nothing much.
Whether what they are carrying is about work at all.

label: Curiosity
name: What's something you've been curious about lately?
description: Positions them as active and alive, not performing. Works as a natural growth-oriented opener.

hints.text: Ask it genuinely. Curiosity questions die if they sound like a test.
Whether the curiosity is near their work or far from it.
Whether they have had any room for it recently.

label: Learning about yourself
name: What have you been learning about yourself recently?
description: Signals interest in them as a human, not just their output. Reflective, non-evaluative.

hints.text: Ask it, then give it real time. It is a slow question.
Whether they answer about a skill or about how they operate.
Whether the learning came from something that went badly.

label: Bring it up
name: Is there something you've been wanting to bring up?
description: Amy Edmondson: explicit space for withheld speech is the most powerful safety-building move a leader can make.

hints.text: Ask early, so whatever it is shapes the rest of the conversation.
Whether they take it, or say no and then circle back later.
How long they have been sitting on it.

label: How you're arriving
name: How are you arriving today?
description: Acknowledges people come from somewhere. Grounding, non-evaluative — makes space before the conversation starts.

hints.text: Ask about right now, this hour. Not the week.
Whether they are actually present or still in the last meeting.
Whether they name a state or default to fine.

label: Most like yourself
name: When have you felt most like yourself recently?
description: Authentic self-concept research. Identity-based, not performance-based. Deep without being intrusive.

hints.text: Ask for a moment, not a period. A specific occasion is easier to answer.
Whether the moment is at work or outside it.
What they were doing when it happened.

label: Looking forward
name: Before we get into specifics, what's been most on your mind about where you're heading?
description: Growth-native opener. Forward-leaning, lets the report frame their own trajectory before manager introduces concerns.

hints.text: Ask before any specifics. Their framing should set the agenda.
Whether they think in roles, skills, or scope.
Whether the direction is theirs or inherited from someone else.

label: Where you are
name: What would you want me to understand about where you are right now?
description: Rogers' empathic understanding made explicit. Positions the manager as a receiver, not evaluator.

hints.text: Ask it as a real request. You are handing them the frame.
What they most want on the record.
Whether they are correcting an impression they think you hold.

label: Outside of work
name: What's been the best part of your world outside of work lately?
description: Explicitly non-work. Kim Scott's 'care personally' — shows genuine interest in the whole person.

hints.text: Ask it and stay out of it. No follow-up needed unless they offer.
Whether there is a life with room in it, or not much to report.
Whether the answer is recent or from a while ago.

label: Time is yours
name: This time is yours. What would you like to do with it?
description: The most honest version of 'I'm here for you'. Makes explicit that the 1:1 belongs to them.

hints.text: Say it and then genuinely hand it over. Do not steer for the first minute.
Whether they use it or hand it straight back.
What they spend it on when it is theirs.

label: Anything to cover
name: Before we start, is there anything specific you want to make sure we cover today?
description: Manager-led check that the report has agenda input before the prepared questions begin.

hints.text: Ask before your agenda, and write theirs down in front of them.
Whether they name something you had not planned for.
Whether it is the thing they actually care about, or a warm-up.
